input.quote: 10.3 Assignment. This Agreement shall be binding upon, and shall inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by, the parties hereto and their respective legal representatives, successors and assigns, but no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 10.3 is the only assignment provision in the Agreement (searches for "assign", "transfer", "consent", "change of control", "merger/affiliate/substantially all" return nothing else; Section 4.1 termination and Section 4.2 termination payment contain no change-of-control trigger). As drafted it is pure boilerplate: it binds successors and assigns but grants no affirmative assignment right, imposes no consent requirement or notice mechanic, and therefore leaves HDI free to assign the Agreement — including to Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled or another competitor named in the Section 6 exclusivity provisions, and with it our Confidential Information, Marks licence and customer e-mail list rights. That fails the fallback on three material terms: successor assignment on written notice, a consent gate for other assignments, and a reasonableness standard on that consent. We therefore propose the preferred position at the same location: an affiliate/successor carve-out for the Company (material here because the parties are affiliated and the Company may be sold), consent (not unreasonably withheld) plus a competitor bar on HDI assignment, and express confirmation that a change of control of the Company gives HDI no termination right. We have kept the existing successors-and-assigns sentence intact and added one sentence group rather than rewriting the clause; the mutual-notice fallback remains available if HDI resists the competitor bar.

mappings.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.

proposal.summary: Add customer affiliate/successor assignment carve-out, consent gate and competitor bar on HDI assignment, and no HDI termination right on the Company's change of control.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 10.3 is a bare successors-and-assigns clause: it leaves HDI free to assign the Agreement to anyone, including a competitor of ours, and does not confirm our own affiliate/M&A assignment rights. We have added our standard assignment position — free assignment by the Company to an affiliate or successor, HDI assignment only with our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to a competitor, and no HDI termination right on a change of control of the Company. If helpful, we can instead accept a mutual successor-assignment right on written notice with consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.

ops.text: The Company may assign this Agreement, without HDI's consent, to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets. HDI may not assign this Agreement without the Company's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, and shall never assign to a competitor of the Company. A change of control of the Company shall not give HDI any right to terminate this Agreement.
